Ressources eduscol : https://eduscol.education.gouv.fr/5850/programmes-et-ressources-en-serie-std2a.
points: A design brief in English follows a clear and predictable structure.
It starts with the context and the name of the client.
The aim states what the project should achieve.
The target audience describes who will use the product.
Requirements list what the solution must do.
Constraints describe the limits : budget, time, materials and regulations.
Deliverables name the expected outputs : sketches, mock-ups and final files.
Short sentences and bullet points improve readability.
A portfolio presents projects with images, a short text and the role of the designer.
Each portfolio entry explains the problem, the process and the result.
Action verbs such as designed, tested and improved show personal involvement.
Proofreading and consistent vocabulary give a professional impression.

questions.q: Which section states what the project should achieve ?
questions.correction: The aim gives the objective of the project.

questions.q: What does 'target audience' mean ?
options: The people who will use the product
questions.correction: The target audience is the group of intended users.

questions.q: Which of these is a constraint ?
questions.correction: Budget, time and materials are typical constraints.

questions.q: What are deliverables ?
options: The expected outputs of the project
questions.correction: Deliverables are what the designer must hand in.

questions.q: Which verb shows personal involvement in a portfolio ?
questions.correction: Action verbs such as designed or tested show what the designer did.

questions.q: What improves the readability of a brief ?
questions.correction: Short sentences and bullet points make the document easier to scan.

questions.q: What should a portfolio entry explain ?
options: The problem, the process and the result
questions.correction: It should show the situation, the work done and what was obtained.

questions.q: Write a short design brief in English for a reusable water bottle.
questions.reponse: Client: City Sports Club. Context: members need a light bottle for training. Aim: design a reusable bottle that is easy to carry and simple to clean. Target audience: young adults aged 18 to 30. Requirements: capacity of 500 ml, no plastic waste, one-hand opening. Constraints: budget of 15 euros per unit, production of 500 pieces, recycled stainless steel. Deliverables: three sketches, one 3D model, one prototype and a short report. Deadline: six weeks.
questions.correction: The answer should include context, aim, audience, requirements, constraints and deliverables.

questions.q: How should you present a project in a portfolio to show your personal role?
questions.reponse: Start with the name of the project and one image that gives the main idea. Then write a short paragraph with the context and the aim. Use action verbs in the first person or in the passive with clarity: 'I analysed the brief', 'I tested three options', 'the final shape was selected after user feedback'. Add one or two process images to show the research and the iterations. Finish with the result and what you learned. Keep the same structure for every project so that the reader can compare them easily. Proofread carefully: spelling mistakes reduce the professional impression, even when the design work is strong.
questions.correction: The expected answer mentions structure, action verbs, process images and proofreading.

fiches.source: Programmes officiels de la serie STD2A (sciences et technologies du design et des arts appliques) : arrete du 8 fevrier 2011 (NOR MENE1104094A, BO special n° 3 du 17 mars 2011) fixant le programme de design et arts appliques du cycle terminal ; arrete du 17 janvier 2019 fixant le programme des enseignements de specialite de premiere et terminale STD2A (design et metiers d'art, analyse et methode en design, conception et creation en design et metiers d'art), BO special n° 1 du 22 janvier 2019 ; arrete du 8 fevrier 2011 (NOR MENE1104152A) pour les mathematiques de premiere STD2A ; programmes de francais, histoire-geographie, anglais, EMC et philosophie des classes de 2nde, 1re et terminale technologique (Bulletin officiel special). points: A design presentation in English needs a clear structure and simple sentences.
Open with the aim of the project and the name of the client.
Signposting expressions guide the audience through the talk.
Use firstly, then, after that and finally to mark the stages.
Present the research before the final solution.
Explain the choices with because and in order to.
Mention the constraints and how the solution answers them.
Show prototypes and explain what each test revealed.
Use however to introduce a limitation honestly.
Invite questions with 'Do you have any questions?' or 'What do you think?'.
Answer a question by listening first, then answering precisely.
Practise pronunciation and timing before the real presentation.

questions.q: How should a presentation open ?
options: With the aim and the client
questions.correction: Stating the aim and the client gives the audience an immediate frame.

questions.q: Which word is a signposting expression ?
questions.correction: Firstly, then and finally mark the stages of the talk.

questions.q: Which linker introduces a limitation ?
questions.correction: However introduces a contrast or an honest limitation.

questions.q: Which sentence explains a purpose ?
options: It is designed in order to reduce waste
questions.correction: In order to + verb expresses the purpose of a choice.

questions.q: When should you show prototypes ?
options: During the presentation, with the test results
questions.correction: Prototypes and their results support the explanation of choices.

questions.q: How to answer a question from the audience ?
questions.correction: Listening first avoids answering a different question.

questions.q: Why practise timing ?
options: To speak as fast as possible
To fit the allotted time and keep the structure
questions.correction: Rehearsal ensures that the essential points are presented within the time.

questions.q: Write the opening and the signposting of a short design presentation.
questions.reponse: Good morning. My name is Leo and I am going to present a portable lamp for students. The client is a company that wants a light made of recycled materials. My aim today is to show how the brief led to the final shape. Firstly, I will present the context and the constraints. Then I will show two prototypes and explain the tests. After that, I will compare the options and justify the chosen solution. Finally, I will mention the limitations and invite your questions.
questions.correction: The answer should include the aim, the client and at least three signposting expressions.

questions.q: How to defend a design choice in English when a limitation is mentioned ?
questions.reponse: Acknowledge the limitation first with a calm phrase such as 'That is a fair point'. Then explain the context: 'We chose this material in order to reduce weight, although it is less resistant than metal.' Give evidence from the process, for example a test result or a comparison between two prototypes. If you agree with the criticism, say what you would improve with more time: 'With a larger budget, I would test a stronger coating.' Finish by linking back to the aim of the project. Keep sentences short, look at the person who asked the question and avoid reading your notes. This structure shows that you can evaluate your work critically rather than simply defend it.
questions.correction: The expected answer uses however or although, evidence, a possible improvement and eye contact.

affichage.texte: Presenting in English means structuring the talk, justifying choices and treating questions as a dialogue.

affichage.eq: Aim → research → prototypes → choice → limitations → questions
